answer: Tree Depth Decay locks the network into a hollow core where new nodes attach only to existing branches. The system traces each connection back to a single willow root node, ensuring no two agents claim the same parent. This architecture forms a dense grove that requires linear effort to fake. To add a duplicate agent, an attacker must craft unique chain histories from the root, which consumes real bandwidth and storage. Each fake node thus costs tangible resources that exceed the value of the stolen transaction. The topology itself acts as the ledger, making false identity expensive.
